In LISP, the function returns the list that results after the first element is removed (the rest of the list), is
(i) car
(ii) last
(iii) cons
(iv) cdr

Output segments of artificial intelligence programming contain
(i) printed language and synthesized speech
(ii) manipulation of physical object
(iii) locomotion
(iv) All of the above

What is artificial intelligence?
(i) Putting your intelligence into computer
(ii) Programming with your own intelligence
(iii) Making a machine intelligent
(iv) Playing a game

Which is not the commonly used programming language for AI?
(i) Prolog
(ii) Java
(iii) LISP
(iv) Perl

An 'agent' is
(i) anything that perceives its environment through sensors and acting upon that environment through actuators
(ii) anything that takes input from the surroundings and uses its intelligence and performs the desired operations
(iii) an embedded program controlling line following robot
(iv) All of the above

What is rational at any given time depends on?
(i) The performance measure that defines the criterion of success
(ii) The agent's prior knowledge of the environment
(iii) The actions that the agent can perform
(iv) All of the above

Weak AI is
(i) the embodiment of human intellectual capabilities within a computer
(ii) a set of computer programs that produces output that would be considered to reflect intelligence if it were generated by humans
(iii) the study of mental faculties using mental models implemented on a computer
(iv) All of the above

Decision tree is
(i) a flowchart
(ii) a structure in which internal node represents test on an attribute, each branch represents outcome of test and each leaf node represents class label
(iii) the flowchart and structure in which internal node represents test on an attribute, each branch represents outcome of test and each leaf node represents class label
(iv) None of the above

Decision nodes are represented by
(i) disks
(ii) squares
(iii) circles
(iv) triangles

Treatment chosen by doctor for a patient for a disease is based on
(i) only current symptoms
(ii) current symptoms plus some knowledge from the textbooks
(iii) current symptoms plus some knowledge from the textbooks plus experience
(iv) All of the above

questions.text: Consider the Water Jug problem as stated here. "You are given two jugs, a 4-gallon one and a 3-gallon one. Neither has any measuring markers on it. There is a pump that can be used to fill the jugs with water. How can you get exactly 2 gallons of water into the 4-gallon jug?" Represent this as a problem in State Space Search and state its Production Rules. Show at least one solution to this problem.

Write a Prolog program that verifies whether an input list is a palindrome.
Hint : Goal : Palindrome ([r, a, c, e, c, a, r])
Output : Yes
Goal : Palindrome ([a, b, c])
Output : No

Decide whether the following statements are true or false. If true, explain why. If false, give a contradicting example. Recall that $B$ is the average branching factor and $L$ is the length of the shortest path from start to goal :
(a) Bidirectional BFS is always faster than BFS when $B \ge 2$ and $L \ge 4$.
(b) $A^*$ search always expands fewer nodes than DFS does.
(c) For any search space, there is always an admissible and consistent $A^*$ heuristic.
(d) $IDA^*$ does not need a priority queue as in $A^*$, but can use the program stack in a recursive implementation as in DFS.

sub_questions.text: Bidirectional BFS is always faster than BFS when $B \ge 2$ and $L \ge 4$.
$A^*$ search always expands fewer nodes than DFS does.
For any search space, there is always an admissible and consistent $A^*$ heuristic.
$IDA^*$ does not need a priority queue as in $A^*$, but can use the program stack in a recursive implementation as in DFS.
